# Specific Heat of UO2 at Elevated Temperature

The specific heat capacity of uranium dioxide (UO2) increases monotonically with temperature. At 300 K, the specific heat of stoichiometric UO2 is 0.300 J/(g K). At 1500 K, it rises to 0.340 J/(g K). The density is 10.97 g/cm^3.

# Heat Capacity Model

The heat capacity follows the Maier-Kelley model with parameters fitted to experimental data. The lattice constant at 1500 K expands to 5.498 angstrom from the 300 K value of 5.4704 angstrom. The melting point of UO2 is 3120 K. The thermal conductivity at 1500 K is 2.5 W/(m K).
